title: Articles: a / an / the
explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds. Use 'the' when both speakers know which specific thing is meant. Use no article for general plural or uncountable nouns.
structure: a + consonant sound | an + vowel sound | the + specific noun

examples.text: I bought a book and an umbrella.
examples.translation: 本と傘を一つずつ買いました。

examples.text: The sun rises in the east.
examples.translation: 太陽は東から昇ります。

examples.text: Dogs are loyal animals.
examples.translation: 犬は忠実な動物です。

commonMistakes: 'An university' is wrong because university starts with a /j/ sound. Say 'a university'.

title: Be verb: am / is / are
explanation: The verb 'be' links a subject to a description, identity, or location. It changes form with the subject and tense.

examples.text: She is a nurse.
examples.translation: 彼女は看護師です。

examples.text: We are ready now.
examples.translation: 私たちもう準備できています。

examples.text: They were late yesterday.
examples.translation: 彼らは昨日遅れていました。

commonMistakes: Do not add another main verb: 'He is like football' -> 'He likes football'.

title: Present simple
explanation: Use the present simple for habits, facts, and general truths. Add -s or -es for he/she/it.

examples.text: I drink tea every morning.
examples.translation: 毎朝紅茶を飲みます。

examples.text: He works at a bank.
examples.translation: 彼は銀行で働いています。

examples.text: Water boils at 100 degrees.
examples.translation: 水は100度で沸騰します。

commonMistakes: Forgetting third-person -s: 'She go to school' -> 'She goes to school'.

title: Questions with do / does
explanation: Form yes/no questions by putting do or does before the subject. Wh-questions add a question word at the front.
structure: Do/Does + subject + base verb? | Wh-word + do/does + subject + base verb?

examples.text: Do you like jazz?
examples.translation: ジャズはお好きですか。

examples.text: Does she live nearby?
examples.translation: 彼女はこの近くに住んでいますか。

examples.text: Where do you work?
examples.translation: どこでお仕事されていますか。

commonMistakes: Keep only one marked verb: 'Does he likes it?' -> 'Does he like it?'.

title: Past simple
explanation: Use the past simple for finished actions. Regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs change form and must be memorised.

examples.text: We visited Osaka last spring.
examples.translation: 去年の春大阪を訪れました。

examples.text: She bought a new laptop.
examples.translation: 彼女は新しいノートパソコンを買った。

examples.text: They did not agree at first.
examples.translation: 最初は同意しなかった。

commonMistakes: Double marking: 'Did you went?' -> 'Did you go?'.

title: Comparatives and superlatives
explanation: Use -er/more to compare two things and -est/most for three or more. Short adjectives take -er/-est; longer ones take more/most.
structure: adj-er + than | more + adj + than | the + adj-est | the most + adj

examples.text: This box is heavier than that one.
examples.translation: この箱の方があの箱より重い。

examples.text: It is the most interesting film I know.
examples.translation: 知っている中で最も面白い映画です。

title: Present perfect
explanation: Use have/has + past participle for past events with present relevance, life experience, or unfinished time periods.

examples.text: I have lived here for five years.
examples.translation: ここに住んで五年になります。

examples.text: She has never eaten sushi.
examples.translation: 彼女は食べたことがありません。

examples.text: Have you finished yet?
examples.translation: もう終わりましたか。

commonMistakes: Do not use finished time words: 'I have seen it yesterday' -> 'I saw it yesterday'.

title: Future: will vs going to
explanation: Use will for instant decisions, promises and predictions. Use be going to for plans already made or evidence-based predictions.
structure: will + base verb | be going to + base verb

examples.text: I will help you carry that.
examples.translation: それを持つのを手伝いますよ。

examples.text: We are going to launch it in June.
examples.translation: 6月に発売する予定です。

examples.text: Look at those clouds - it is going to rain.
examples.translation: あの雲を見て、雨が降りそうだ。

commonMistakes: 'I will to call you' is wrong; will takes the bare infinitive: 'I will call you'.

title: Passive voice
explanation: Form the passive with be + past participle to focus on the action or when the agent is unknown or unimportant.
structure: Subject + be (any tense) + past participle (+ by agent)

examples.text: The bridge was built in 1912.
examples.translation: この橋は1912年に建てられた。

examples.text: Mistakes will be corrected.
examples.translation: 間違いは訂正されます。

examples.text: English is spoken worldwide.
examples.translation: 英語は世界中で話されています。

commonMistakes: Keep the correct form of be for each tense: 'was wrote' -> 'was written'.

title: Relative clauses
explanation: Use who for people, which for things, that for either, and where for places to add information without starting a new sentence.

examples.text: The teacher who explains clearly is popular.
examples.translation: わかりやすく説明する先生に人気があります。

examples.text: This is the cafe that my sister recommended.
examples.translation: これは姉がお勧めしたカフェです。

commonMistakes: Do not double the subject: 'The book which I read it' -> 'The book which I read'.

title: Conditionals (zero and first)
explanation: Zero conditional states general results; first conditional states likely future results of a real condition. The if-clause uses present tense even about the future.
structure: if + present, present | if + present, will + base verb

examples.text: If you heat ice, it melts.
examples.translation: 氷を加熱すると溶けます。

examples.text: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay in.
examples.translation: 明日雨なら家にいます。

commonMistakes: Never put will inside the if-clause: 'If it will rain' -> 'If it rains'.

title: Gerunds and infinitives
explanation: Some verbs take a gerund (-ing) and others take an infinitive (to + verb). The choice is fixed by the main verb and must be learned together.

examples.text: She enjoys reading novels.
examples.translation: 彼女は小説を読むのを楽しみます。

examples.text: They decided to move abroad.
examples.translation: 彼らは海外に移ることに決めました。

examples.text: Stop to smoke and stop smoking mean different things.
examples.translation: stop to smoke と stop smoking は意味が大きく変わります。

commonMistakes: 'I look forward to see you' is wrong; the to is a preposition: 'look forward to seeing you'.

title: Reported speech
explanation: When reporting what someone said, shift tenses back one step and adjust pronouns and time expressions.

examples.text: She said she was tired.
examples.translation: 彼女は疲れたと言った。

examples.text: He told me he would call later.
examples.translation: 後で電話すると言われました。

commonMistakes: Backshift consistently: 'He said he is busy yesterday' -> 'He said he had been busy'.

title: Second and third conditionals
explanation: Second conditional imagines unlikely present situations; third conditional regrets impossible past situations.
structure: if + past simple, would + base verb | if + past perfect, would have + past participle

examples.text: If I had more time, I would learn piano.
examples.translation: 時間がもっとあったならピアノを習うのに。

examples.text: If she had studied, she would have passed.
examples.translation: 勉強していたなら合格していたでしょう。

commonMistakes: Match the halves: mixing second and third forms produces unclear meaning.

title: Inversion after negative adverbials
explanation: When a negative or restrictive adverbial opens a sentence, invert subject and auxiliary for emphasis (formal style).

examples.text: Never have I seen such precision.
examples.translation: これほど精密なものを見たことがありません。

examples.text: Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.
examples.translation: 彼女は勝っただけでなく記録も更新した。

commonMistakes: Keep normal order after mid-sentence adverbs: 'She never has...' is fine too.

title: Subjunctive mood
explanation: Use the base form after verbs of demanding, suggesting, insisting, and in set phrases expressing wishes or hypotheticals.

examples.text: I suggest that he study harder.
examples.translation: 彼がもっと勉強すべきだと提案します。

examples.text: If I were you, I would accept.
examples.translation: あなたの立場なら受け入れます。

commonMistakes: Do not add -s in the that-clause in formal AmE: 'suggest that she study', not 'studies'.
